Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Overview and Core Approach

The Labour Party's 2024 manifesto presents a plan centered on five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, expanding opportunity, and NHS reform. The document emphasizes fiscal responsibility, with commitments to balance day-to-day spending with revenues and reduce debt as a share of the economy.

## Economic Policy

Labour proposes establishing an Industrial Strategy Council to guide long-term economic planning across sectors including financial services, automotive, life sciences, and creative industries. A National Wealth Fund would receive £7.3 billion to invest in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, and green hydrogen production.

The party commits to capping corporation tax at 25%, maintaining full expensing for capital investment, and reforming business rates. Planning reform features prominently, with targets of 1.5 million new homes over the parliament, including restoration of mandatory housing targets and strategic greenbelt release.

Devolution would expand through new powers for combined authorities over transport, skills, housing, and employment support. Local Growth Plans would be developed with employers and educational institutions.

## Energy and Environment

The manifesto targets clean electricity by 2030 through doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind. Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, would receive £8.3 billion in capital.

On North Sea oil and gas, Labour would not revoke existing licenses but would cease issuing new exploration licenses. The windfall tax on energy companies would be extended and increased. A Warm Homes Plan would invest £6.6 billion to upgrade five million homes.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and establishing specialist rape units in every police force. The party would bring rail services into public ownership as contracts expire.

Education proposals include 6,500 new teachers funded by ending VAT exemptions for private schools, free breakfast clubs in primary schools, and 3,000 new nurseries in primary school buildings. A curriculum review would be conducted.

## Immigration and Security

A Border Security Command would replace the Rwanda scheme, with counter-terrorism-style powers to target smuggling networks. The party would seek a security agreement with the EU for intelligence sharing. Additional caseworkers would address asylum backlogs, and a returns unit with 1,000 staff would expedite removals.

Defence commitments include maintaining the nuclear deterrent, NATO membership, and conducting a Strategic Defence Review with a path to 2.5% GDP spending.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposed changes include removing hereditary peers from the House of Lords, introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for peers, extending voting rights to 16-17 year olds, and establishing an Ethics and Integrity Commission. The party would reset relationships with devolved governments through a new Council of the Nations and Regions.

## Funding

Revenue measures include closing non-dom tax status loopholes, ending private equity carried interest treatment as capital gains, extending energy windfall taxes, and modernizing HMRC enforcement. Spending efficiencies would come from halving consultancy costs, police collaboration programs, and ending asylum hotel use.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto centres on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expand apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The manifesto commits to responsible fiscal management while repairing trade relationships with Europe. Tax proposals include reversing bank tax cuts, increasing the Digital Services Tax, and reforming capital gains tax.

## Health and Social Care

Central pledges include guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and ensuring NHS dental access for emergency care. Mental health provisions include walk-in hubs for young people and professionals in every school. The party proposes free personal care based on the Scottish model, a Royal College of Care Workers, and increased Carer's Allowance with expanded eligibility.

## Education

Proposals include placing mental health professionals in all schools, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment would include extra free hours for disadvantaged three and four-year-olds.

## Environment

The manifesto commits to net zero by 2045, with 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home energy upgrade programme would provide free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households. Water companies would be transformed into public benefit companies, with bonuses banned until sewage discharges end. Targets include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing

The party would build 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities. Renters would receive protection through banned no-fault evictions and three-year default tenancies. Rough sleeping would be ended within the Parliament.

## Crime and Justice

Proposals include restoring community policing, guaranteeing police attendance at all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. Court backlogs would be addressed through increased investment, with rehabilitation programmes expanded to reduce reoffending.

## Immigration

The party would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish safe legal routes for refugees, and process asylum claims within three months. Asylum seekers could work after three months of waiting. Work visa policy would move from the Home Office to relevant departments.

## Democratic Reform

Key reforms include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, scrapping voter ID requirements, and capping political donations. The Ministerial Code would become law, and House of Lords reform would proceed.

## International Affairs

The manifesto prioritises repairing EU relations through a four-stage roadmap, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership. Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, Army cuts would be reversed, and international development spending would return to 0.7% of national income. The party supports Ukraine and advocates for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza with recognition of Palestinian statehood.

## Families and Welfare

Proposals include extending free school meals to all children in poverty, doubling Statutory Maternity Pay to £350 weekly, and removing the two-child benefit limit. The triple lock on pensions would be maintained, and compensation for 1950s-born women would be delivered.
